quotes: A metabolic myopathy associated with chronic lactic acidemia, growth failure, and nerve deafness.

records.label: 23-year-old male

phenotypes.text: mitochondrial abnormalities on muscle electron microscopy

quotes: Clinical, biochemical and pathological findings are described in a 23-year-old male with a mitochondrial myopathy who had a high-output circulatory state and cardiomyopathy which resulted in cardiac insufficiency 22 years before presentation of the skeletal myopathy.
Venous lactate levels were elevated and severe lactic acidosis developed at one stage of the illness.
Electron microscopy of muscle tissue showed various mitochondrial abnormalities and accumulation of neutral lipids which was confirmed histochemically and by thin-layer chromatography.

quotes: She was compound heterozygous for two frameshift mutations, p.Asn112HisfsX29 and p.Leu659AlafsX4, in the PNPLA8 gene

Segregation analysis confirmed that the variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. In addition, genotyping of two healthy siblings revealed they were negative for both variants.
At age 2, she was noted to have a positive Gowers sign, and by the age of 3 years could no longer walk.

Brain MRI showed microcephaly with simplified gyral pattern, hypoplasia of corpus callosum, prominent cisterna magna with hypoplastic cerebellum, brainstem atrophy (Figure 2A–C).

records.segregation: c.2275_2276del maternally inherited; variants in trans; father unavailable; both variants in affected sister
quotes: Sibling A is currently a 49-year-old man. His first symptoms occurred at the age of 14 years when he developed weakness and distal muscle atrophy of his lower limbs.
Sibling A became nonambulant at the age of 44 years. A neurologic examination at the age of 45 years showed mild dysarthria and horizontal nystagmus.

The previously described c.2275_2276del variant was maternally inherited. Unfortunately, the paternal DNA sample could not be obtained for segregation analysis, but results of whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing allowed us to ascertain that both changes were on different alleles (in trans) (Figure 1, B and C).

quotes: Sibling B developed difficulty in walking and weakness in both lower limbs at the age of 14 years.

Coordination testing revealed severe axial ataxia and appendicular dysmetria, which was more pronounced in the lower limbs. She was unable to maintain an upright posture. Cranial nerve examination and cognitive evaluation were normal.
The presence of these variants was confirmed in the affected sister by Sanger sequencing.

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) reviewed 25 affected individuals from 20 families with biallelic PNPLA8 variants and concluded that PNPLA8-related neurological disease forms a continuum from developmental and/or degenerative epileptic-dyskinetic encephalopathy with congenital microcephaly to childhood-onset neurodegeneration.
quotes: Analysis of the clinical features of current and previously reported individuals (25 affected individuals across 20 families) showed that PNPLA8-related neurological diseases manifest as a continuum ranging from variable developmental and/or degenerative epileptic-dyskinetic encephalopathy to childhood-onset neurodegeneration.

notes.statement: Among their 14 new patients, Nakamura et al. (2024) found central hypotonia (13/13), dystonia (8/12), seizures (10/14) and cerebellar atrophy (12/12). The 8 severe patients had congenital microcephaly (5/7), no developmental milestones, early-onset seizures, simplified gyri, pontocerebellar hypoplasia and progressive cerebral atrophy.
quotes: Highly frequent clinical features of our patients were central hypotonia (100%, 13/13), dystonia (67%, 8/12), seizure (71%, 10/14) and cerebellar atrophy (100%, 12/12).

Neuroimaging revealed that these patients showed a simplified gyral pattern (100%, 6/6), pontocerebellar hypoplasia (100%, 7/7) and severe progressive atrophy of the cerebral cortex (100%, 5/5; Fig. 1E–R).

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found that biallelic loss-of-function variants affecting 3 or 4 PNPLA8 protein isoforms were associated with the severe end of the spectrum. Patients with the mild, late-onset movement disorder phenotype all carried biallelic C-terminal frameshift variants (p.Thr757Glnfs*10 or p.Leu759Alafs*4), which were thought to escape nonsense-mediated decay and leave residual protein.
quotes: Regarding their genotypes, biallelic LoF variants affecting three or four PNPLA8 protein isoforms were associated specifically with this group (Fig. 2).
All the patients in this group harboured biallelic C-terminal frameshift variants (p.Thr757Glnfs*10 or p.Leu759Alafs*4) (Fig. 2).
the C-terminal truncating variant is likely to avoid NMD and lead to less severe clinical manifestations

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) showed that the c.1625+3_1625+6del variant caused skipping of exons 6 to 8 and that fibroblasts from the patient had markedly reduced 77-kDa PNPLA8. A missense variant from a previously reported severe patient (homozygous p.Val520Asp) gave normal protein levels.
quotes: Sequencing of each separated transcript by TA cloning revealed that c.1625+3_1625+6del resulted in the skipping of exons 6–8 owing to aberrant splicing

the missense variant identified in the previously reported patient (severe phenotype with homozygous p.Val520Asp) resulted in a similar protein expression level to the controls despite the severe phenotype

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found that cardiolipin and monolysocardiolipin levels appeared lower in patient skin fibroblasts than in controls, without a significant correlation with phenotypic severity. Fibroblasts from 1 severely affected patient had reduced maximal mitochondrial respiration but normal mitochondrial morphology.
quotes: Although a significant correlation was not observed between CL/MLCL abundance and phenotypic severity, the abundance of CL and MLCL appeared to be decreased in patient-derived skin fibroblasts compared with control samples
Transmission electron microscopy analysis did not reveal altered mitochondrial morphology in the patient-derived skin fibroblasts

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found that PNPLA8-knockout and patient-derived iPSC cerebral organoids had a smaller subventricular zone, fewer PAX6+HOPX+ basal radial glial cells and fewer SATB2+ upper-layer neurons. Deep-layer neurons and basal intermediate progenitors were unchanged. The authors suggested an altered S phase in apical radial glia.
quotes: The number of PAX6+HOPX+ bRGCs in the SVZ was significantly reduced in PNPLA8 KO cerebral organoids compared with WT cerebral organoids (Fig. 4A and B).

The number of SATB2+ upper-layer neurons was significantly reduced in Patient 1-derived cerebral organoids compared with Control cerebral organoids, but there was no significant difference in the number of CTIP2+ deep-layer neurons

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found that PNPLA8-knockout neural progenitor cells had reduced lysophosphatidic acid, lysophosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidic acid, with normal mitochondrial function and cardiolipin. Adding lysophosphatidic acid partly restored the number of basal radial glial cells in patient-derived organoids.
quotes: The amounts of LPA, LPE and PA were decreased in PNPLA8 KO NPCs compared with WT NPCs, whereas there was no significant difference in that of other phospholipids and free fatty acids (Fig. 7E).
Treatment with LPA increased the number of bRGCs in Patient 1-derived cerebral organoids (Fig. 7F and G).

notes.statement: Using spatial transcriptomics of the ventricular zone in patient-derived organoids, Nakamura et al. (2024) found enrichment of cell-cycle, neuronal differentiation and lysophospholipid pathway gene sets and depletion of basal radial glia gene sets. They suggested that loss of PNPLA8 alters the fate specification of apical radial glia.
quotes: we found that gene sets related to ‘Neocortex basal radial glia-up’ and ‘Human neocortex’ were much less enriched in Patient 1-derived cerebral organoids (Fig. 6E and F).
revealed ‘lysophospholipid pathway’ as the top-ranked enrichment only in the VZ of Patient 1-derived cerebral organoids

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) identified homozygous N-terminal frameshift PNPLA8 variants, affecting only the 88-kDa isoform, in 2 Iranian patients from a non-neurological cohort, 1 with optic atrophy and 1 with nonsyndromic hearing loss. An affected sib in the optic atrophy family was heterozygous, so the authors considered the significance of these variants undetermined.
quotes: These findings indicate the undetermined significance of these N-terminal frameshift variants, although biallelic LoF variants in PNPLA8 have been linked to neurological diseases.

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found that all 14 PNPLA8 variants identified in their patients had frequencies below 0.001% in population databases.
quotes: the frequency of all of the variants was <0.001%, suggesting a strong purification effect attributable to disease pathogenicity

notes.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) proposed infantile onset as a new, distinct phenotype of PNPLA8-related disease. They suggested that the site of the variant, rather than its type, was strongly correlated with age at onset, and that the PNPLA8-related conditions formed a spectrum of overlapping features that line up with different ages of onset.
quotes: our results add the infantile onset as a new distinct phenotype of the disease and suggest that the site of the variant rather than its type is strongly correlated with the disease onset
these conditions demonstrate some overlapping features representing a spectrum with clinical features always aligning with different age of onset

notes.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) noted that biallelic PNPLA8 variants had been described with three presentations: a congenital form (congenital microcephaly, early-onset epileptic encephalopathy and early death), childhood neurodegeneration with progressive microcephaly, and adult-onset cerebellar ataxia with peripheral neuropathy. Only six patients had been reported before their study.
quotes: Pathogenic variants in PNPLA8 have been described either with congenital onset displaying congenital microcephaly, early onset epileptic encephalopathy and early lethality or childhood neurodegeneration with progressive microcephaly.
a phenotype comprising adulthood onset cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy was also reported
only six patients with biallelic variants in PNPLA8 have been reported so far

notes.statement: Burnyte et al. (2023) noted that both PNPLA8 truncating variants in their sibs lay in the last coding exon, suggesting that such transcripts may escape nonsense-mediated decay and possibly retain partial enzyme activity, resulting in a less severe phenotype than the severe early-childhood neurodegeneration reported with c.2275_2276del in trans with another truncating variant.
quotes: Both protein-truncating variants were identified in the last coding exon of PNPLA8 gene, suggesting that such transcripts may escape nonsense-mediated decay and possibly result in preserved partial enzyme activity and less severe clinical manifestation.

Of interest, c.2275_2276del has been reported in a compound heterozygous state with other variant leading to protein truncation and resulting in severe neurodegeneration manifesting in early childhood.

notes.statement: Burnyte et al. (2023) described a milder PNPLA8-associated phenotype in 2 adult sibs with adolescent-onset cerebellar ataxia and sensorimotor polyneuropathy that advanced markedly in the teens but progressed only slightly in adulthood, with preserved cognition and without visual, auditory, cardiac, or liver dysfunction.
quotes: Both patients manifest a unique course of cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy with a remarkable advance in their teens but only a slight progression throughout adulthood.
Both patients avoided a decline in cognitive function and typical systemic manifestations including visual, auditory, cardiac, and liver dysfunctions.

notes.statement: Masih et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing in a patient with prenatal-onset severe progressive neurodegeneration who died in infancy. They identified a novel homozygous missense variant in PNPLA8 (c.1874A>G) located in the patatin domain.
quotes: Using whole-exome sequencing, we identified a homozygous novel missense variation c.1874A>G in the patatin domain of PNPLA8.
The patient had prenatal-onset severe and progressive neurodegeneration with mortality in infancy.

notes.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) described 2 unrelated girls with biallelic loss-of-function PNPLA8 variants who had variable but similar features of microcephaly, severe global developmental delay, spasticity, lactic acidosis, and progressive cerebellar atrophy. They considered the condition a progressive neurodegenerative mitochondrial disorder, with one patient presenting at birth with congenital microcephaly and seizures and the other showing regression after normal development until 13 months.
quotes: we report two unrelated individuals with variable but similar clinical features of microcephaly, severe global developmental delay, spasticity, lactic acidosis, and progressive cerebellar atrophy with biallelic loss-of-function variants in PNPLA8.
P1 presented in the newborn period with congenital microcephaly, spasticity and seizures. However, P2 had normal development till one year followed by neuro-regression

notes.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) noted that all PNPLA8 variants reported to date introduce premature stop codons. Because so few patients were known, they concluded that no genotype-phenotype correlation could be drawn.
quotes: The variants observed in PNPLA8, including the ones in our study are loss-of-function pathogenic variants, which introduce a premature stop codon (Figure 1E).
due to limited number of individuals, a genotype-phenotype correlation cannot be deduced at present.

notes.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) found by Western blot of muscle from the patient a dramatic decrease of the 88-, 63-, and 52-kD PNPLA8 (iPLA2-gamma) bands compared with control muscle samples, consistent with a null genotype.
quotes: Western blot showing dramatic decrease of the 88, 63, and 52kD PNPLA8 protein (NP_001242940.1) in the muscle from CMH193, compared to muscle from three control samples with known non-mitochondrial diagnoses.

notes.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) noted that the clinical features and the mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities in their patient closely resembled those of Pnpla8-null mice, which have mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired learning, decreased exercise endurance, a thin body habitus, and cold intolerance.
quotes: The Pnpla8 -/- mouse has mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired learning, decreased exercise endurance, enhanced insulin sensitivity, a thin body habitus (from energy dissipation by mitochondrial uncoupling), and cold intolerance.

notes.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) found normal SDH and COX activity and unaffected electron transport chain function in patient muscle, and suggested that altered inner mitochondrial membrane homeostasis, rather than a primary respiratory chain defect, underlies PNPLA8-related disease.
quotes: oxidative enzyme reactions (SDH and COX) showed normal activity in muscle (Supp. Figure S1), and electron transport chain function was not affected (Supp. Table S1).

This may also be the case with PNPLA8-related disease, where proteins involved in electron transport and ATP synthesis located in the inner membranes would be secondarily affected by altered membrane homeostasis but not the primary pathogenic mechanism.

notes.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) reported that both PNPLA8 variants were absent from the Exome Sequencing Project and an internal database of 1,913 samples, and that homozygous truncating PNPLA8 variants were absent.
quotes: Both PNPLA8 variants were absent from the NHLBI Exome Sequencing Project (EVS; http://evs.gs.washington.edu/EVS/) and an internal variant database of 1913 samples. Truncating PNPLA8 variants were absent from the internal dataset and rare in the EVS, and homozygous truncating variants were absent.

notes.statement: Mancuso et al. (2009) found that iPLA2-gamma-null mice had profound alterations in hippocampal phospholipid metabolism. These included markedly elevated hippocampal cardiolipin with a shift to shorter-chain molecular species, decreased plasmenylethanolamine content, increased oxidized phosphatidylethanolamine species, and increased ceramides.
quotes: Shotgun lipidomics demonstrated multiple alterations in hippocampal lipid metabolism in iPLA(2)gamma(-/-) mice including: 1) a markedly elevated hippocampal cardiolipin content with an altered molecular species composition characterized by a shift to shorter chain length molecular species
including a decreased plasmenylethanolamine content; 3) increased oxidized phosphatidylethanolamine molecular species; and 4) an increased content of ceramides.

notes.statement: Mancuso et al. (2009) found enlarged heteromorphic lamellar structures undergoing degeneration in the hippocampus of iPLA2-gamma-null mice, together with ubiquitin-positive spheroid inclusion bodies. Purification and proteomics identified these structures as degenerating mitochondria. The authors concluded that loss of iPLA2-gamma causes a mitochondrial neurodegenerative disorder with autophagy and cognitive dysfunction.
quotes: Electron microscopic examination demonstrated the presence of enlarged heteromorphic lamellar structures undergoing degeneration accompanied by the presence of ubiquitin positive spheroid inclusion bodies.
identified them as degenerating mitochondria
iPLA(2)gamma loss of function results in a mitochondrial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by degenerating mitochondria, autophagy, and cognitive dysfunction.

notes.statement: Mastaglia et al. (1980) observed marked improvement in the myopathy of their patient after starting prednisone and thiamine, and the improvement persisted after these drugs were withdrawn.
quotes: Marked improvement in the myopathy occurred after commencement of prednisone and thiamine and was maintained following withdrawal of these drugs.

notes.statement: Mastaglia et al. (1980) did not define the metabolic defect in their patient. They proposed that an abnormality in the Krebs cycle caused the overproduction of lactate and the lipid accumulation in muscle.
quotes: The metabolic defect in this case has not been defined, but an abnormality in the Kreb's over-production of lactate and lipid accumulation in muscle is postulated.
